primary_issue: The shatter event and brick impact are not clearly staged or energetic: the brick isn’t readable striking the center from the left, and there’s no convincing outward shard eruption / debris field to sell a high-speed impact.
issues: Brick/impact readability is poor (brick appears tiny/unclear and not centered; trajectory does not read as left-to-right center strike).
Shatter lacks force and drama: minimal outward eruption, weak momentum, sparse debris field.
Fracture pattern reads artificial/simplistic (flat polygonal shards, limited branching/micro-fragmentation, weak thickness/edge definition).
Lighting is flat and unmotivated for a gritty cinematic night warehouse; shards don’t sparkle/catch strong highlights.
Environment/materials are underdeveloped (wall/frame look like basic gray shaders; little rust/grime/aged concrete variation).
Composition deemphasizes the action (window too small in frame; large dark bars/foreground elements dominate and distract).
Some elements look smeared/soft without purposeful motion blur; overall glass/material separation is muddy.
Remaining glass doesn’t convincingly crack-and-collapse from the frame (reads mostly like a partially fractured pane still in place).
suggestions: Re-compose so the window/impact occupies ~40–60% of frame; remove/relocate the large dark foreground bars/occluders that steal focus.
Make the brick unmistakable: increase apparent size/readability, ensure it crosses the pane center from the left; add strong directional motion blur (and shard motion blur) to sell speed.
Increase fracture complexity and shard count: denser radial cracks + more small fragments + broader outward spread; ensure visible thickness and bright specular edge catches.
Material tuning (glass): reduce tint/murk so glass reads cleaner and edges pop. Try lowering absorption density (Line 290: 0.12 → ~0.04–0.07) and keep IOR plausible (Line 285: 1.52 OK).
Fracture/shard granularity: increase Voronoi detail for smaller pieces (Line 327: voro Scale 8.0 → ~14–20) to avoid big flat chunks (assuming this drives fracture cell size).

Improve gritty warehouse feel via texture breakup: increase procedural texture frequency/variation (Line 155: noise_a Scale 6.0 → ~10–14; Line 161: noise_b Scale 25.0 → ~35–60; adjust roughness variation accordingly) and add obvious rust/grime layers on the frame/wall.

Add motivated cinematic lighting: increase environment/background contribution and shape it so shards get crisp highlights. Try raising background strength (Line 75: 0.12 → ~0.3–0.8) and then re-balance exposure/contrast so the scene isn’t uniformly dim.
Make the ‘remaining glass collapses’ read: detach/sag sections near the impact and lower edge; add secondary dust/tiny debris to reinforce impact energy (kept subtle).
vision_assessment: The image reads as a dim, sparse CG warehouse-like wall with a small window area showing partial breakage. The primary action is not immediately legible: the supposed brick is hard to identify and does not read as a heavy red clay brick striking the center from the left. The glass break pattern looks stylized and under-detailed (few large, dark, flat-looking shards), with little sense of a violent outward explosion of fragments. Lighting and materials are flat; glass highlights are weak, and the concrete/metal lack convincing age, rust, and grime. Composition and foreground shapes distract from the window, further reducing the cinematic impact.
